gap: No result ChatGPT got states that FOPO sells a 15.3-inch triple extender with 1920×1200 panels, the S980, or how it connects; I could not source its video path today, because FOPO's product page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt.
standout_why: I compared four pages. UPERFECT's '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders' (cited) has no 15.3- or 15.6-inch 1920×1200 model. Its only Mac note is that base M1 and M2 MacBooks support one external display, and it never says 'Alt Mode' or 'DisplayLink'. Dealectric's own 16-inch page (cited) covers the S11, S9G, Trio 3 Pro and S788, but nothing 15-inch and not the S980. I could not open the Newegg Hyangin Z3 page (cited; HTTP 403), so I can't say what it states about compatibility. FOPO's S788 page (cited) is FOPO's 16-inch model. The one new thing I could source is that the S980 exists, which fits the shopper's 15-inch size, but not its compatibility cells. So the finding is only partly new for this angle.
decides: This doesn't decide the pick yet. The FOPO S980 is the only product in our partner stores that matches the question's size (15.3 inches) and resolution (1920×1200). It is in stock at FOPO's US store. Whether it can be the pick, or only the pick for one segment, depends on its video path. A driver-based three-screen unit like the S788 runs on base M1–M3 Macs but blocks protected video. A native unit needs one video-capable output per screen, which leaves out base M1 and M2 MacBooks. A later run needs to open the S980 page when FOPO stops rate-limiting. If its three screens need a driver, it matches the S788 on compatibility and wins on size. If only two screens are needed, the S11 (native, excludes base M1/M2/M3 per FOPO as quoted on Dealectric's page) and the S9G stay the 16-inch alternatives.
